career-troubleshooting-058.rule: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Welke stap; heeft is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Gaan/zullen plus a bare infinitive can announce the next action. Bezig zijn met names an ongoing task, not its completion.

career-troubleshooting-059.rule: Bezig with an activity. The first constituent is Ik; ben is the finite (conjugated) verb and Ik is its subject. In a declarative main clause, the finite verb is second in constituents, not necessarily second in individual words. A finite form of zijn plus bezig describes an ongoing activity. Met takes an activity noun/nominalised infinitive; a te-infinitive construction names the action directly. Do not confuse met with the conjunction terwijl. Gaan/zullen plus a bare infinitive can announce the next action. Bezig zijn met names an ongoing task, not its completion.

career-troubleshooting-060.rule: Fronted subordinate clause. The first constituent is Als deze test niets oplevert,; vragen is the finite (conjugated) verb and we is its subject. In a declarative main clause, the finite verb is second in constituents, not necessarily second in individual words. The complete subordinate clause counts as the first constituent of the main clause. The main finite verb follows it, then the main subject. Inside the subordinate clause its own verb/group comes toward the end. Gaan/zullen plus a bare infinitive can announce the next action. Bezig zijn met names an ongoing task, not its completion.
